amount of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

sentences.text:
That on 17.01.2023 at about 08.40 PM., the petitioner was riding the vehicle bearing reg No.KA-64-J- 5942, near 4th cross, Gundappa Layout, Nagasandra, Bengaluru,
wherein the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MT-0079 drove it, with high speed, rash and negligent manner that is without showing signal or putting indicator and dashed against two wheeler and caused the accident.

In the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries, he was shifted to K.C.General Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient for accidental injuries sustained by him and he was discharged on 20.01.2023.
Petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards his medical expenses.
He stated that due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to perform his work as earlier.

Prior to the accident the he was hale and healthy and he is aged about 34 years and he was doing plumber work and thereby he was earning Rs.45,000/- per month.
Further petitioner stated that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle which belongs to respondent no.2 who insured his vehicle with respondent no.1 and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.22/2023 against the driver of the offending vehicle.
He prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel, filed Vakalath and written statement by denying the entire petition averments in toto.

Respondent No.2 being owner has not chosen to contest the petition and he placed ex-party.
4.
Respondent No.1 contended that there is delay of five days in lodging the complaint and the petitioner has implanted the vehicle with an intention to claim the compensation.
Further he contended that as per IMV report no damages is found on the insured vehicle and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
5. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and examined another 2 witness as PW.2 and PW3 and got marked 25 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 25 and they are fully cross examined.

Respondent No.1 has not chosen to lead the evidence, there is no material on record to show that respondent No.1 is prevented from leading the evidence, hence respondent No.1 evidence is taken as nil.
6. I have heard the arguments for the counsel appearing for both the sides and I have perused the entire records.

7. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioner proves that on 17.01.2023 at about 08.40 PM., he was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA-64-J-5942 on 4 th cross, Gundappa Layout, Nagasandra, wherein the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-02-MT-0079 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident as alleged in the petition?
Kumar.

PW1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, wound certificate, IMV report, Final report, Intimation to the police, MLC register extract which are at Ex.P.1, 2, 6 to 8, 11,
20 and 21.
10.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that respondent No.2 being the driver of offending vehicle and the accident took place due to his rash and negligent act.
Ex.P.6 is the wound certificate it reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries that is fracture of right knee.
Ex.P.12 is the discharge summary, it shows that the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for 8 days and surgery was done for his right patellar knee fracture at KC General Govt Hospital, Bengaluru.
11. In the cross examination of the PW-1 he clearly deposed that the accident had occurred due to the negligent act of the respondent No.2, he deposed that he is having valid driving license.
Nothing worth has been elicited from the mouth of the PW-1 to disprove his version and to probabilise their contention as contended in the written statement.

Apparently there is 5 days delay in filing the complaint and complainant being the petitioner, he has assigned the reason in the complaint which is at Ex.P.2 that he was taking treatment at KC General hospital and he give the complaint to Peenya Traffic police station after consulting his family members
. The said fact is also whispered in the FIR which is at Ex.P1.
Considering the facts and attending circumstances and the injuries sustained by the petitioners the aforesaid reasons for the delay has to be accepted.
Respondent No.1 has failed to probabilise his contention that petitioner has falsely implanted the vehicle in the accident.
Respondent No.1 has not chosen to examine the IO of this case, nor challenged the final report which is at Ex.P.11.
Final report is filed after through investigation and it cannot be brush aside.
Inasmuch respondent No.1 version cannot accepted without any tantamount evidence.
Kumar.

12. Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, discharge summary the said documents shows that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries that is fracture of right knee and he took treatment as inpatient for 8 days and he was discharged on 25.01.2023.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, Medicines,
Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
13.
Petitioner took treatment at KC General Govt hospital Bangalore.
He has tendered the wound certificate, discharge summary and medical receipts along with the related documents.
On perusal of the same it is apparent that, surgery was done for his right patellar knee fracture on 20.01.2023.
Evidently nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve the medical bills.
Accordingly the wound certificate, discharge summary has to be accepted.
Admittedly he has taken treatment for 8 days, for attendant charges, transportation, nourishing food, he might have spend some more expenses.
Therefore - I award Rs.20,000/-. compensation under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.
14. The petitioner has not substantiated the established his nature of his work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place on 17.01.2023, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2023 is Rs.15,500/-, and same is assessed and considered as his monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that at-least one month, he has lost his income.
Therefore I award Rs.15,500/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
15. The petitioner has examined the doctor S.A.Somashekar, working as an orthopedic surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru as PW-3.
He deposed that, petitioner has 18% of whole body disability as per Ex.P24 and it is not functional disability.
16. PW-3 in his cross examination, deposed that he has not treated the petitioner, fracture is united and implants are in the body of the petitioner.
Ex . P.20
is the MLC register extract, Ex.P.21 is the intimation to the police reveals that the intimation of accident is intimated to the jurisdictional police at the earliest point of time.
Ex.P.14 is the DL of the petitioner.
Ex.P.7 is the IMV report of two wheeler related to the petitioner, wherein the damages are stated by the concerned authority.

Ex.P.2 is the complaint wherein the petitioner has clearly explained that he was taken treatment for accidental injuries as such he could not given the complaint to the Peenya Traffic police station as on the date of the incident.
Evidently the aforesaid facts can not disbelieved in view of Ex.P.20 and 21 and medical documents tendered by the petitioner.
17. Learned counsel for the respondent No.1 argued that the aforesaid disability cannot be considered as whole body disability and the said assessment of PW-3 is on higher side.

I have perused the evidence of PW-3 wound certificate, discharge summary, Ex.P6 and 12 which includes Kumar.K vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60459160/
4 X-ray, surgical notes and reports and it corroborates with oral testimony of PW-3.

sentences.text: Nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW-3 to disprove the said investigations, reports made for the disability assessment of petitioner.
Evidently petitioner has not examined the doctor who has treated him in the Govt hospital.
It is true that fracture is united, considering the medical reports and oral testimony of PW-3, the whole body disability of the petitioner is assessed as 6%.
18. The notional monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.15,500/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 36 years as per the entry in Aadhar card which is at Ex P.13.
The multiplier applicable to this case is "15".

Therefore loss of income on account of permanent disability is calculated as follows; Rs.15,500/-(Monthly income) X 12 (Months) X 15 ( Multiplier) X6%
(Functional Disability) = Rs.1,67,400/-,
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.1,67,400/- as compensation under this head.

Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
19.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injury and it is grievous in nature.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings.
There fore I award Rs.20,000/- under this head.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
20.
The petitioner has to forgone certain amenities available for him.

Therefore I award Rs.20,000/-
as compensation under this head.
21. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.
In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

Sl Particulars Amount  No.
 1 Towards attendant charges, Rs.20,000/-
 transportation, nourishing food  2 Loss of income during the laid up period Rs.15,500/-
 3 Loss of income on account of Rs.1,67,400/-
 permanent disability  4 pain & sufferings Rs. 20,000/-
 5 loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/-
22 . Rate of Interest:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s
Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% P.a.

Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.a. on the compensation am Kumar.K vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60459160/
